newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's low interest rates must be maintained - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan's low interest rates must be maintained - EPA.

text.p: Japan's policy of low interest rates must be maintained for the time being to support the economy, newly appointed Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso said on Friday.
Aso told foreign news agencies in an interview that Japan's economic recovery is likely to become self-sustainable in the next fiscal year starting April 1.
He also said rapid fluctuations in foreign exchange rates cause trouble for Japan's economy, and added that currency rates must not move too rapidly.
"It is necessary for major nations to maintain cooperation in stabilising exchange rates rather than push exchange rates to a certain level," he said.
Aso said he personally thinks that a rise in interest rates sometimes helps push up spending by consumers who depend on income from interest rate payments.
"However, I think low interest rates must be maintained and be given priority for the time being to support the economy," he added.
A planned rise in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from the current three percent next April is expected to have a limited impact on consumer spending, he said.
"If I were asked about the possibility of Japan's economy contracting next fiscal year, I would bet that there wasn't such a possibility," he said.
